To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Philadelphia chromosome (Ph1), the t(9;22) translocation, is the aetiological lesion in chronic myeloid (or myelogenous) leukaemia, that the BCR–ABL oncogene is the aetiolethal gene in CML and that imatinib mesilate is a potent inhibitor of the BCR– ABL tyrosine kinase.

(i) CML is a clonal disease of haemopoietic stem cells that is initiated by a single genetic lesion, a chromosomal translocation between chromosome 9 and chromosome 22, the so-called Philadelphia chromosome, that leads to the expression of a novel protein tyrosine kinase, BCR-ABL, which is constitutively activated and drives the clonal expansion and survival of leukaemic stem cells; (ii) BCR-ABL is a potent oncogene
imatinib mesilate, an inhibitor of the Abl kinase, is effective in the treatment of chronic myeloid leukemia.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the identification and characterisation of the genetic lesions responsible for the development of cancer, with the development of new therapies based on these discoveries, and with the application of these new therapies in the clinic.
the molecular mechanisms of normal haemopoiesis and leukaemogenesis and the development of new therapeutic strategies.
the molecular pathogenesis of cancer and the translation of this research into new and better cancer treatments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the introduction of imatinibs mesylate into clinical practice heralds a new era in cancer therapeutics.
imatinib meslyate has been registered for the treatment of CML, a disease that is caused by a single genetic lesion, the Philadelphia (Ph) chromosome.
imatinib mesilate is a new and highly active agent in the treatment of chronic phase CML that is refractory to interferon-α.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are now able to cure a disease that we previously could not cure.
we have identified the first oncogene that can be effectively targeted by a specific inhibitor.

the identification of the BCR-ABL oncogene and its role in CML led us to the identification of a small molecule that can inhibit the activity of the oncogene product and thus the development of the leukaemia.
The main takeaway from our work is that
imatinib mesy-late is a very promising agent for the treatment of CML and that it has a role in the management of other malignancies.
imatinib mesilate is a very effective treatment for CML.
imatinib mesyate is a potent inhibitor of the tyrosine kinase activity of the Bcr-Abl protein.
